9.desc: Blue Zushi is a slightly indica dominant hybrid strain created through crossing the delicious Zkittlez X Kush Mints strains. Known for its gorgeous appearance and pretty well balanced high, Blue Zushi is perfect for any indica lover. This bud has small and fluffy rounded forest green nugs with deep blue undertones, vivid orange hairs and a thick frosty coating of gorgeous tiny blue-tinted white crystal trichomes. As you pull apart each sparkling little nugget, aromas of spicy flowers and rich earthy pine are released, almost like walking through a forest after a rainstorm. The flavor is of sweet earth and spicy flowers with a mellow herbal tea-like taste that lingers on the tongue. The Blue Zushi high comes on with a slow sneaking creep, sneaking into you before launching you into a lifted and energized state. You'll feel a budding euphoria accompanied by a tingly buzzy body high that quickly makes your energy level u-turn into deep relaxation and ease.

The Big Sur Holy Weed – Sage single pre-roll is a thoughtfully crafted collaboration that blends High Grass Farms’ precise cultivation with the soulful, heritage-driven identity of Belushi’s Farm. True to its name, Sage delivers a fresh, herbal aroma that stands apart from sweeter or gas-heavy profiles. Notes of pine, earth, and classic green herbs lead the nose, while the smoke remains smooth and balanced with a crisp, botanical finish. The flavor feels natural and grounding, appealing to consumers who appreciate old-school cannabis expressions and terpene profiles that lean earthy and aromatic.

The effects are typically calming and centered, offering a relaxed, clear-headed experience that eases tension without overwhelming the senses. Many enjoy Sage for daytime or early-evening use, as it promotes a mellow body feel while maintaining mental clarity. In this 1g single pre-roll, Big Sur Holy Weed – Sage delivers a purposeful, well-rounded experience that reflects the craftsmanship and philosophy behind both High Grass Farms and Belushi’s Farm.

518.desc: Durban Poison has deep roots in the Sativa landrace gene pool. The strain’s historic phenotypes were first noticed in the late 1970s by one of America’s first International strain hunters, Ed Rosenthal. According to cultivation legend, Rosenthal was in South Africa in search of new genetics and ran across a fast flowering strain in the port city of Durban. After arriving home in the U.S., Rosenthal conducted his own selective breeding process on his recently imported seeds, then begin sharing. Rosenthal gave Mel Frank some of his new South African seeds, and the rest was cannabis history. Frank, who wrote the “Marijuana Grower’s Guide Deluxe" in 1978, modified the gene pool to increase resin content and decrease the flowering time. In search of a short-season varietal that could hit full maturation on the U.S. East Coast, Frank’s crossbreeding efforts resulted in two distinct phenotypes, the “A” line and “B” line. The plant from Frank’s “A” line became today’s Durban Poison, while the “B” line was handed off to Amsterdam breeder David Watson, also known as “Sam the Skunkman.” Durban Poison has a dense, compact bud structure that’s typical of landrace Indica varieties, but the flowers’ elongated and conical shape is more characteristic of a Sativa.
